title: The Rebuilding of the Ka'bah and the Placement of the Black Stone
overview: This episode covers the major events in the life of Prophet Muhammad ⌨ around the age of 35, highlighting the virtues of Khadijah رنها and the Prophet's children. It details the decision of Quraysh to rebuild the Ka'bah using only pure halal funds, which led to altering its structure and excluding Hijr Ismail. Finally, it recounts the Prophet's ⌨ brilliant wisdom in resolving a bitter dispute among the tribes over placing the Black Stone.
lessons: A successful marriage requires mutual affection, respect, and loyalty that endures even beyond death.
Sacred work must be funded by clean, halal earnings; dirty money has no place in noble endeavors.
True wisdom (hikmah) requires leaders to forego optimal actions if implementing them would cause widespread confusion or fitnah among the people.
Effective conflict resolution restores unity by giving every aggrieved party a shared sense of honor and ownership.

chapters.title: The Devotion and Status of Khadijah (radiyallahu 'anha)
chapters.summary: The lecture opens with reflections on the 25-year marriage of Prophet Muhammad ⌨ and Khadijah رنها, noting that no arguments or disputes were ever recorded between them. Among all the Ummahat al-Mu'minin, Khadijah holds a unique position as the Prophet's first wife, with whom he shared his longest marriage without taking other wives. Even long after her passing, the Prophet ⌨ remembered her with profound affection, regularly sending gifts of meat to her friends. When her sister Halah bint Khuwaylid visited Madinah, her voice reminded him of Khadijah, leading A'ishah رنها to express natural jealousy. In response, the Prophet ⌨ swore by Allah that none replaced her, praising Khadijah's firm belief when others disbelieved and her financial and emotional support.
key_points: The marriage of Prophet Muhammad ⌨ and Khadijah lasted 25 years without a single recorded argument.
The Prophet ⌨ maintained Khadijah's memory by sending portions of slaughtered sheep to her lifelong friends.
A visit from Halah bint Khuwaylid in Madinah prompted the Prophet ⌨ to express deep nostalgia for Khadijah.
In response to A'ishah's jealousy, the Prophet ⌨ declared: 'Wallahi ma abdalanillahu khayran minha' ('Allah did not replace her with someone better').

chapters.title: The Prophet's Children and the Four Perfect Women
chapters.summary: Khadijah رنها was the mother of six of the Prophet's seven children, including two sons (al-Qasim and Abdullah) and four daughters (Ruqayyah, Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah). The Prophet's title Abu al-Qasim was derived from his eldest son, a kunyah reserved exclusively for him. Abdullah was also affectionately known by the nicknames al-Tayyib and al-Tahir. Later in Madinah, the Prophet ⌨ had another son named Ibrahim with Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah. The chapter concludes with the famous Hadith identifying the four women who reached spiritual perfection: Asiyah (the wife of Fir'awn), Maryam bint 'Imran, Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, and Fatimah bint Muhammad.
key_points: Khadijah bore six children: al-Qasim, Abdullah, Ruqayyah, Zaynab, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah.
Muslims may name their children Muhammad or Qasim, but using the kunyah Abu al-Qasim is reserved exclusively for the Prophet ⌨.
Abdullah was nicknamed al-Tayyib (the good one) and al-Tahir (the pure one).
The Prophet ⌨ named four women who achieved spiritual perfection (kamal): Asiyah, Maryam bint 'Imran, Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, and Fatimah bint Muhammad.

chapters.title: The Quraysh Resolve to Rebuild the Ka'bah
chapters.summary: When Prophet Muhammad ⌨ was 35 years old—five years prior to the first revelation—a major flood and a local fire damaged the structure of the Ka'bah. A woman carrying incense (bukhor) accidentally set fire to the Kiswah, weakening the stone walls and creating fear of an imminent collapse. Quraysh faced major logistical challenges, as they lacked expertise in building with stone or wood, and lacked sufficient funds. Providentially, a wooden ship was wrecked at the port of Jiddah, allowing Quraysh to purchase its timber for the ceiling. Simultaneously, slave traders brought a Roman slave to Makkah who was an expert in stone masonry, which Quraysh saw as divine assistance for their project.
key_points: The rebuilding occurred when Prophet Muhammad ⌨ was 35 years old.
The Ka'bah was severely weakened by a heavy flood in Makkah and an accidental fire involving the Kiswah.
Quraysh lacked construction experience with stone bricks and wooden roofs.
A ship shipwrecked at Jiddah provided timber, and a Roman slave skilled in stone masonry provided construction expertise.

chapters.title: Pure Wealth and Structural Limitations
chapters.summary: Quraysh established a strict rule that the Ka'bah could only be rebuilt using 100% pure, halal money. They explicitly banned any contributions derived from prostitution or interest (riba), recognizing even in Jahiliyyah that such earnings were dirty. This standard exposed the reality that most merchant wealth in Makkah was impure, leaving the leaders with insufficient funds. Faced with the choice of accepting dirty money or shortening the sanctuary, they chose to maintain the purity of the project. Consequently, they reduced the surface area of the Ka'bah, leaving out the curved wall section known today as Hijr Ismail.
key_points: Quraysh stipulated that only pure funds free from prostitution and interest (riba) could be used to rebuild the Ka'bah.
The condition revealed that much of Makkah's commercial wealth was considered impure.
Rather than compromise the sanctuary with dirty money, Quraysh chose to reduce the surface area of the structure.
The excluded curved section was enclosed by a low wall and named Hijr Ismail.

chapters.title: Demolition and the Green Stone Foundations
chapters.summary: Before construction could begin, the old structure of the Ka'bah had to be demolished. The leaders of Quraysh hesitated out of fear, remembering the divine punishment that befell Abrahah's army 35 years earlier when they tried to destroy the Ka'bah. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah reassured them that their intention was noble, prayed to Allah for understanding, and struck the first blow. When no harm came to him overnight, the rest of Quraysh joined the demolition. While excavating the foundation, they reached green stones laid by Prophet Ibrahim عليه السلام. When a worker struck one of the green stones, a blinding light flashed and an earthquake shook Makkah, prompting them to leave Ibrahim's foundation intact.
key_points: Quraysh leaders hesitated to demolish the walls out of fear of divine punishment similar to the Year of the Elephant.
Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah initiated the demolition after praying and declaring their good intention.
Excavations reached the original green stone foundation laid by Prophet Ibrahim عليه السلام.
Attempting to move a green stone caused a blinding light and a tremor across Makkah, leading them to preserve the base.

chapters.title: Structural Changes and Prophetic Wisdom
chapters.summary: Quraysh completed the building in a square cube shape, marking the excluded curved wall area as Hijr Ismail so pilgrims would know it was part of the original sanctuary. Anyone performing tawaf must walk around Hijr Ismail for their circumambulation to be valid. Additionally, Quraysh reduced the doors from two to one and elevated the remaining door to restrict entry. Years later, after the Conquest of Makkah, Prophet Muhammad ⌨ told A'ishah رنها that were it not for her people being new to Islam, he would have restored the Ka'bah to Ibrahim's original design, demonstrating his immense wisdom in preventing public confusion and fitnah.
key_points: Hijr Ismail remains an integral part of the Ka'bah; circumambulation (tawaf) must pass outside it to be valid.
Quraysh elevated the single entrance door to control access into the Ka'bah.
After the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ⌨ refrained from rebuilding the Ka'bah on Ibrahimi foundations to avoid confusing new Muslims.

chapters.title: Historical Alterations and Imam Malik's Advice
chapters.summary: During the conflict between Abdullah ibn Zubayr and al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf, catapult attacks damaged the Ka'bah. Ibn Zubayr rebuilt the structure according to the original Ibrahimi plan, incorporating Hijr Ismail and adding two ground-level doors. However, after defeating Ibn Zubayr, al-Hajjaj demolished his additions and restored the Qurayshi design. When Khalifah Abdul Malik ibn Marwan learned of the Hadith and intended to rebuild it back to Ibn Zubayr's design, Imam Malik ibn Anas advised him against it. Imam Malik warned that altering the Ka'bah with every new ruler would turn the sacred house into a political toy, a principle respected to this day.
key_points: Abdullah ibn Zubayr rebuilt the Ka'bah incorporating Hijr Ismail and two ground-level doors.
Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf reversed Ibn Zubayr's modifications after conquering Makkah.
Imam Malik ibn Anas advised Khalifah Abdul Malik ibn Marwan not to alter the structure again.
Imam Malik argued that the Ka'bah should not become a tool or toy in the hands of successive rulers.

chapters.title: Resolving the Dispute over al-Hajar al-Aswad
chapters.summary: As rebuilding neared completion, a fierce dispute arose among the sub-tribes of Quraysh over who would have the honor of placing the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad). Clans like Banu Abd al-Dar and Banu Makhzum dipped their hands in vessels of blood, swearing to fight to the death for the privilege. Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah proposed that the next person to enter Bab Bani Shaybah should arbitrate. When Muhammad ⌨ walked through the gate, they rejoiced, calling him 'al-Sadiq al-Amin'. The Prophet ⌨ placed the stone on a cloak and had a representative from each clan lift a corner together, before placing it into the wall with his own hands.
key_points: Clans such as Banu Abd al-Dar and Banu Makhzum swore oaths over blood to win the honor of placing the Black Stone.
Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah suggested using the first person entering Bab Bani Shaybah as an arbitrator.
Upon seeing Muhammad ⌨, the tribal leaders exclaimed: 'al-Sadiq al-Amin! Radina!' ('The truthful, trustworthy one! We are content!').
The Prophet ⌨ unified the clans by having all leaders lift the cloth carrying the stone together.

Rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī wa ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wanfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]], we will pick up from where we left off last week.
Last week, we spoke about the marriage of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ to [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة بنت خُوَيْلِد]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
And this was a blessed marriage.
And it was a beautiful marriage that we still take lessons from today.

Any couple who wants to know how to live a happily married life should look at the marriage between [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ and [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
There are no accounts at all during the 25 years that they were married,
there are no accounts at all of any type of arguments that they had, or any type of dispute, or any type of fighting, no account whatsoever.
So they had a very, very beautiful married life where they both respected each other, and they showed each other mutual love and compassion as husbands and wives should do.
So it was a beautiful marriage, and [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she has a special place even amongst the wives of the Prophet ﷺ.
And all of them, all of the wives of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ are [[Ummahat al-Mu'minin|أمهات المؤمنين]].
They are our mothers. They are the mothers of the believers, as Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] Himself has declared them as such.
The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers. So all of the wives of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ are our mothers.

And they all deserve our honor and our respect. But even amongst the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she has a special standing.
She was the first wife of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ. He was married to her for the longest time, for longer than he was married to any of his other wives.
While he was married to her, he didn't marry any other woman. During the time he was married to her, she was his only wife.
And these are blessings that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave to [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
And even after she passed away, the Prophet ﷺ was very sad upon her passing.
And even after she passed away, he continued to honor her, and he continued to show his love for her
by making sure that he kept in contact with her friends.
Whenever he would sacrifice a sheep, he would make sure that some portion of that meat, it goes to the friends of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
This is how he remembered her even after she had passed away.
One time, the sister of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], her name was [[Halah bint Khuwaylid|هالة بنت خويلد]],
and the way that she would ask permission to enter the home was similar to the way of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
You know how sometimes siblings, they have a similar way of speaking and a similar way of doing things,
so [[Halah bint Khuwaylid|هالة بنت خويلد]] had a similar way of asking permission to enter the home as [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] used to have.
So one time [[Halah bint Khuwaylid|هالة بنت خويلد]] came to the house of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

And this was much later, a long time after [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] had passed away, and the Prophet ﷺ was in [[Madinah|مدينة]] now, and he was with [[A'ishah|عائشة]] at this time.

And [[Halah bint Khuwaylid|هالة بنت خويلد]], the sister of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she came to the house of the Prophet ﷺ and asked for permission to enter the house.
And the way that she asked for this permission, it reminded [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].

So when he heard it, when he heard her, he said, "[[Allahumma Halah|اللهم هالة]], [[Allahumma Halah|اللهم هالة]]"—"O Allah, let it be [[Halah bint Khuwaylid|هالة]], let it be [[Halah bint Khuwaylid|هالة]]."
He wanted it to be the sister of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].

And [[A'ishah|عائشة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], she's witnessing this happening, and she felt a little jealous. And of course, it's natural. This jealousy is natural, and it's nothing to be blamed about.
So she felt this jealousy, and she said

to [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, "[[Ya|يَا]] [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]], why do you constantly remember this old woman when Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] has replaced her with someone who is better than her?"
She's talking about herself.
And the Prophet ﷺ upon hearing this, his face changed.
His face changed, and he said, "[[Wallahi ma abdalanillahu khayran minha|والله ما أبدلني الله خيرا منها]]"—"I swear by Allah that Allah did not replace her with better than her.
[[Amanat bi hina kafaran-nas|آمنت بي حين كفر الناس]]. She believed in me when the people, they disbelieved.
[[Wa saddaqatni idh kadhdhabaniyan-nas|وصدقتني إذ كذبني الناس]]. And she believed in my truthfulness when the people were calling me a liar.
[[Wa wasatni bi-maliha|وواستني بمالها]]. And she supported me with her wealth.
[[Wa razaqaniyallahu minhal-walada duna ghayriha minan-nisa'|ورزقني منها الله الولد دون غيرها من النساء]].
And Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave me children through her, unlike the other wives, unlike the other wives of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ."
So this is the position of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] with the Messenger ﷺ.
And as he mentioned, she is the only wife that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] provided children to [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ through her. Later on,
the Prophet ﷺ also had a son, [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]], from [[Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah|مارية القبطية]],
but [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]] was the mother of six of his children.
He had two sons and four daughters with [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].

His son, his first son, his name was [[al-Qasim|القاسم]], and that is where [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ gets his [[kunyah|كُنية]], his title [[Abu al-Qasim|أبو القاسم]], the father of [[al-Qasim|القاسم]], because his first son was named [[al-Qasim|القاسم]].

And the Prophet ﷺ said that we can name our children with his name, meaning you can name your child [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], you can take the name [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], but do not take the [[kunyah|كُنية]] of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

Do not call yourself [[Abu al-Qasim|أبو القاسم]]. You can name your son [[al-Qasim|قاسم]], no problem, but you don't take the [[kunyah|كُنية]] [[Abu al-Qasim|أبو القاسم]]. This is reserved for [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
When you say [[Abu al-Qasim|أبو القاسم]], it means [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

So we can call ourselves [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], we can name ourselves or our children [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], that's fine, but you do not take the [[kunyah|كُنية]] of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, you do not call yourself [[Abu al-Qasim|أبو القاسم]].
This is restricted for [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
So his first son, that was [[al-Qasim|القاسم]]. Then he had another son with [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], and his name was [[Abdullah|عبد الله]].
And [[Abdullah|عبد الله]] also had some nicknames. He was also known as [[al-Tayyib|الطَّيِّب]] and [[al-Tahir|الطَّاهِر]]. His nicknames were [[al-Tayyib|الطَّيِّب]] and [[al-Tahir|الطَّاهِر]].
[[al-Tayyib|الطَّيِّب]] means the good one, and [[al-Tahir|الطَّاهِر]], it means the pure one.

And some people, they make the mistake, they say [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, his sons were [[al-Qasim|القاسم]] and [[Abdullah|عبد الله]] and [[al-Tayyib|الطَّيِّب]] and [[al-Tahir|الطَّاهِر]]. No, this is not correct.

[[Abdullah|عبد الله]] was [[al-Tayyib|الطَّيِّب]], [[Abdullah|عبد الله]] was [[al-Tahir|الطَّاهِر]]. These were just nicknames. So it was [[al-Qasim|القاسم]] and [[Abdullah|عبد الله]]. These were his two sons with [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خَدِيجَة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]].
And he had four daughters as well through that marriage.
And those daughters were [[Ruqayyah|رقية]] and [[Zaynab|زينب]] and [[Umm Kulthum|أم كلثوم]] and [[Fatimah|فاطمة]] [[radiyallahu 'anhunna|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُنَّ]].
Four daughters of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ: [[Ruqayyah|رقية]], [[Zaynab|زينب]], [[Umm Kulthum|أم كلثوم]], and [[Fatimah|فاطمة]] [[radiyallahu 'anhunna|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُنَّ]].
Six children through this marriage, a blessed marriage. And the Prophet ﷺ said
that many men have achieved [[kamal|كمال]], have achieved perfection, and of course he's talking about the Prophets of Allah,
but out of the women, only four women achieved perfection. And of course these four women who achieved perfection, they are not prophets, because all of the prophets are men.
But these four women reached a station unlike any other woman. There were many men who reached a station...
perfection, but only four women.
And he mentioned who these four women were:
[[Asiyah|آسِيَة]], [[zawjatu Fir'awn|زوجة فرعون]],
[[Asiyah|آسِيَة]], the wife of [[Fir'awn|فرعون]],
[[Maryam bint 'Imran|مريم بنت عمران]],
[[Maryam bint 'Imran|مريم]], the daughter of [['Imran|عمران]],
that's the mother of [[Isa ibn Maryam|عيسى بن مريم]]
[[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]],
and [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة بنت خويلد]], [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]],
and [[Fatimah|فاطمة بنت محمد]], [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]].
These are the only four women who have reached the station of perfection:
[[Asiyah|آسِيَة]], the wife of [[Fir'awn|فرعون]],
[[Maryam bint 'Imran|مريم]], the daughter of [['Imran|عمران]], the mother of [[Isa ibn Maryam|عيسى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]],
[[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة بنت خويلد]],
and [[Fatimah|فاطمة بنت محمد]], [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]].
So this again shows the status of [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]], [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]], with [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and with Allah,
that she has a high position with Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] as well.

So this was the state of the marriage of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]], [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]], by all means, a perfect marriage, a perfect marriage.
And into this marriage, about 10 years into the marriage—
and we said last week that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was 25 and [[Khadijah bint Khuwaylid|خديجة]], [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]], she was 40 at the time of this marriage—
about 10 years into the marriage, when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was 35 years old,
so this is just a few years before he's going to receive the first revelation. He received the first revelation:
He received that revelation when he was 40 years old.
So about five years before that, when he was 35 years old,
a very important incident happened in the history of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
This was the year that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] decided to rebuild the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
This is when [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] is about 35 years old.
The leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they get together and they decide, 'We need to rebuild the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].'
Why did they decide to rebuild the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]?
It had become very weak, and they feared that it was so weak, the structure, that it may fall down.
That's how weak the structure had become.
Why did it become weak like that?
Most of the historians say that it was due to a major flood that hit [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
A big flood hit [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is a valley. [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is a valley, it's a low point that is surrounded by mountains.
So whenever there's a big storm or whenever there's heavy rain, the rainwater collects in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So there have been many incidents in history where [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] has gotten flooded. [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] has actually gotten flooded many times in history.
And the last major flood that happened in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] was in the year 1941.
And there are some pictures actually of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] and of the [[Haram|حرم]] during this flood that you can see.
And the [[mataf|مطاف]], the area of [[tawaf|طواف]], it is completely immersed with water, and the water is not just, you know, at your feet level, but it's at a very high level,
to such the extent that people were doing [[tawaf|طواف]] swimming.
And you can see it in pictures.
Go and Google 'Makkah flood 1941', and you will see pictures of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] and around it water is surrounding it and people are swimming doing [[tawaf|طواف]].
So this just happened relatively recently, you know, within the last century.
So from time to time when there's heavy rain, [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] would become flooded.
So most of the historians say that this happened during that time of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
And the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was not very strong at that time to begin with.
So when this rain hit, it damaged the structure such to the extent that it was feared that it may fall down and collapse at any time.

So this is what most of the historians say was the reason why—[[jazakallahu khayran|جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا]]—this is the reason why most of the historians say that [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] decided to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
There is another opinion that some of the historians have, that there was a woman who used to go around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with scent, with [[bukhor|بخور]].
And you know the [[bukhor|بخور]], right? Sometimes brother [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], he comes in the [[masjid|مسجد]] with the [[bukhor|بخور]]. It's lighted on some coals, right?
So if that thing falls down or if it hits something, it can be flammable.
So some of the historians say that what happened is that the woman, she was going around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with the [[bukhor|بخور]] to make the area smell good and fragrant,
and something happened, an accident happened that caused the [[Kiswah|كسوة]] of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], the covering, the cloth covering of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], to catch on fire.
And the fire spread and it actually damaged the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] itself to such an extent that it was almost ready to collapse.
Anyhow, whatever the reason is, whether it was the flood or whether it was the fire,
the point is that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] realized that it's very important and very urgent that they need to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] before it actually collapses and before it falls down.
But there were some problems.
One of the problems was that the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was built with bricks of stone.
The [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was built with stone, and the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], their houses and their buildings that they had experience with building, it was built out of mud—mud and clay.

So they didn't really have experience in construction with stone. It's a different type of construction: constructing with mud bricks and constructing with stone bricks, it's a totally different type of work.

So when [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] when they built the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], they built it with bricks of stone. So the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they didn't have experience with this.
So that was one issue.
Another issue was that they needed to raise enough money to complete this project.
So how were they going to get the money to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]? So these were a couple of the issues.
Also, they wanted to build a ceiling for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] out of wood, and they didn't have experience in building with wood either.
So these were some of the issues that they needed to solve before they could actually embark on the rebuilding.
So they discussed these issues, and they discussed what to do about it.
And during this time, while they were still in these discussions, a ship came to the port of [[Jiddah|جدة]].
And [[Jiddah|جدة]] is not very far away from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. It's about 70 km away from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and [[Jiddah|جدة]] is a port city where the ships come in.
So a ship came into [[Jiddah|جدة]], and that ship beached on the port and it was destroyed.
And that ship was built out of wood.
So the ship was beyond repair when it beached up on the shore, they couldn't repair it. So they decided to just sell the wood.
They decided to go and sell the wood.
So they came with that wood into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] trying to sell it. And the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] said, 'Oh, we need the wood! We need to build the ceiling for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with wood.'
So they saw this as a sign from Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]. 'Look, Allah is making things easy for us. He is providing this wood for us and we need it.'
Another sign that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] was making this project easy for them was that, as we mentioned before, the slave trade was a very common thing going on during this era.
And people would constantly come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with slaves and try to sell those slaves to the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. This was a very common occurrence.
So during this time, when the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] were contemplating how to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], some slave traders came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] with a slave, a Roman slave.
And what was the occupation and the experience of this slave? He happened to be a construction worker whose expertise was in stone bricks.
So they said, 'Oh, look! This is something we don't know how to do, and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] has brought this man to us to help us with this project.'
So they saw these as signs: the wood has come to us, the experience has come to us, so we should go on with this project,
and we should now start to gather the funds to take care of this project.
So they thought to themselves and they discussed among themselves, the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], 'How are we going to finance this? This is not going to be cheap.'
So they decided to open the doors for donations. They decided to allow the public and the common people to donate for this worthy, honorable project.
But they made some very, very strict conditions on who could donate.
They weren't just going to open this up for anyone.
They said, 'The [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], this is the house of Allah, this is the most honorable house of Allah, it is pure, and we will only...'
...only accept pure money to rebuild it. It has to be 100% clean, the money.
So they told the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], "Yes, we're opening it up for donations. If you want to participate in this project, that's great, but the money has to be 100% clean."
So they said, "No money from prostitution." And prostitution was a business in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] at that time.
There were people who used to have women slaves, and they used to rent, [[wa al-iyadhu billah|والعفاذ بالله]], those slaves out for prostitution.
So that was a practice in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] during that time, and they used to earn a lot of money by doing that.
So these leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] said, "Anyone who is earning money through this prostitution, we will not take anything from them."
"Anyone who deals with interest, we're not going to take any money from them." See, look, even in the [[Jahiliyyah|جاهلية]]...
...they knew that interest money is something that is impure.
This was before Islam, but they knew that this is something that is dirty, interest money.
So they said, "Anyone who deals with interest, we're not taking any money from them."
So any type of impure money, basically, they said, "We're not accepting it."
And they opened the door for pure, clean donations.
So what happens in the end? Through this exercise and through these conditions...
...the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they realized that most of the money of the businessmen of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] is dirty money...
...because they only are able to raise a very small amount.
They didn't raise much money at all because of these conditions. So they realized, wow, most of the business of these people, it's a very dirty business.
Their money is not clean. So this truth came to light due to this.
So they collected a small amount of money, not enough for them to do the project fully.
So now they realized that they're going to have a lot of expenses, you know, they're going to have to pay for the materials,
they're going to have to pay for the labor, they're going to have to pay a lot of money,
and they knew that what they had collected from the people was not enough.
So again, they consult amongst themselves, and they say, "Okay, we only have two options here."
"Either we can cancel those conditions and allow for any type of money to come in, and take their dirty money and do the project with that..."
"...or we can rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with the money that we have, but it's not going to be the same size. We're going to have to make it a little bit smaller..."
"...in terms of the surface area. We're going to have to make it smaller because we don't have enough money to build it on the same surface."
So they said, "Okay, what should we do?
Either take the dirty money and do a full job, or keep this clean money that we have and do a job that will not be complete..."
"...will not be able to build it the same way that it is."
So they decided to keep the clean money, because the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] is too honorable to take dirty money for any work regarding it.
So they said, "We'll keep the clean money, and we'll do whatever we can, and we will make the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], we'll build it on a smaller surface area than it is on now."
So that is the decision that they took.
All right. So what is the first step now that they have decided that they are going to actually go through with the project?
The first step is that they need to break down the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
They can't rebuild it unless they break it down.
Imagine a building that's about to collapse. Can you just repair it? No, you have to demolish it and then you have to rebuild it again.
So this was the first step that they needed to take. So they got their tools ready, they got their axes, all these big leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]...
...and they go to the wall of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with their axes, and then they start saying to each other, "Okay, you start."
So then the other guy says, "No, no, you start." "No, no, you start."
So each one of them is too scared to start breaking the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], and they want the other one to do it.
"You do it." "No, you do it." "No, you do it." And it keeps going on like this.
Each one of them is scared. They're terrified to take their axe to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
And why is that?
We said this happened when [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was 35 years old.
So what happened 35 years earlier, the year [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was born?
And many of these people who are here on this day, on that day that they were deciding to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], many of those leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they witnessed,
they were old enough to witness what happened 35 years ago.
They saw it with their own eyes: the incident of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], when [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] came and tried to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].

So these leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], many of them who witnessed with their own eyes what happened in this same place 35 years ago, they're scared now to bring their axe to the wall of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So each one of them is trying to get the other one to start, and nobody wants to do it.
Finally, [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] ibn al-Mughirah...
...[[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] ibn al-Mughirah, he's one of the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and he is the father of Khalid ibn [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]].

So [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] says, "Look, [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s intention was to actually destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. That's not what we're doing here. Our intention is not to destroy the house of Allah."
"Our intention is actually good. We want to rebuild it and make it strong so it doesn't fall down. So you can't compare what we're doing to what [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] did."
So [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]], he tries to reason with them.
And they're very happy actually. They said, "Okay, okay, then you do it. You go ahead and start."
So [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] says, "Okay, okay, no problem. I will start." And then before he starts, he says, "O Allah, You know that our intention here is not to do anything bad.
It's not to destroy Your house. Our intention is good, that we want to rebuild it stronger." And then he starts. He hits it with his axe.
And that is the side of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] between al-Rukn al-Yamani and [[al-Hajar al-Aswad|الحجر الأسود]], between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone, that wall of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]],
that is where [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] takes his axe and he starts to break it. And he breaks it, and he breaks it, and he breaks it, and it starts crumbling down.
Then he tells the people, "Okay, I started. Now, come on, you guys join me."
They said, "No, no, no, no, first we have to wait to see if anything happens to you.
If anything bad happens to you, then, if nothing bad happens, then we'll join you. You can continue, you go ahead."

So [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]], he continues to do it, do it, do it himself. The first day, only [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] is the only one who's doing it. Nobody helps him, they're just sitting watching.

Then the next day, [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]] comes back with his sons to help him, and they start doing it again. This is the second day, nothing has happened to [[Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah|الوَلِيد]], he's fine.
The [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] realize this, they said, "Okay, it seems safe," and they all start to help doing that as well.
And that's how all of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] now started to bring down this weak structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So finally, they break it all down. Now, they need to dig the earth for the foundation. They want to rebuild the foundation as well, to make the foundation strong.
So they dig, and they dig, and they dig, and they dig, they dig very deep...
...until they see some green stones, a number of green-colored stones. And it is said that these green stones, this is the foundation of [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
That is the foundation where [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] started his construction of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So they dig all the way to these green stones.
And when they reach these green stones, they say, "Okay, let's dig even deeper than the green stones, so we'll make the foundation even stronger.
We'll go even more deep than those green stones."
So one of them, one of the people who was digging, he has an axe, and he puts his axe under one of those green stones, and then he propels it up,
you know, to get the stone out so they can continue digging. So once he does this, once he puts his axe under that green stone and pulls it up...
...a blinding light comes out, a light that is so bright that it almost blinded him.
So he's taken aback with the brightness of this light, and he drops his axe, and the stone, it falls back into its place.
And some of the narrations of some of the historians also mention that when he actually moved that stone with his axe, the whole [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it shook.
So when they realized this, when they saw this happening, they said, "Okay, just leave it. We're not going to dig deeper than this. Let us leave it at this foundation."
So they kept the same foundation on those green stones, and they started to rebuild the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
Like we mentioned, the amount of money they had was not enough for them to make the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] on the same surface area as it was. And how was the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] before?
The [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was four sides. It is still four sides. At that time, it was four sides. Three sides had straight walls.
Now, if you see the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] today, all four sides have straight walls, it's like a cube shape.
But at that time, three sides had straight walls, but one side had a curved wall.
one structure with three straight walls and then one curved wall,
one wall that made a shape like a semicircle.
But it was all one building.
So they realized that they're not going to be able to do that, so they made, instead, they made a cube
with three of the walls on the same area,
but then they cut off the last wall that was a, that was a circular wall, and they actually closed it off and made it into a straight wall.
And the area that originally was encompassed by the curved wall, they put a, they put like an arch, like a semicircle there,
so that you know that this originally was part of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. This was actually the fourth wall of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] around here.
So they demarcated that place to make sure that it was known that this was the original structure, and it is still like that today.
When you go to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] today, you see that the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] is a square structure, but on one side, you see that semicircle,
and that is called [[Hijr Ismail|حجر إسماعيل]].
And that is actually, originally, that was part of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. The whole building, the structure of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], actually encompassed that whole area.
But because they didn't have the funds to complete that, the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] is as you see it today,
and they kept that area there to demarcate it so that the people know that this originally, actually, this is part of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] as well.
So that's why it's very important, if you go for [[Umrah|عمرة]] or if you go for [[Hajj|حج]] or if you want to do [[tawaf|طواف]],
you have to make sure that you go around that semicircle. Don't make the mistake and circumambulate only around the cube.
Don't try to cut in to that area between the semicircle and the cube. Don't try to cut into that area and make [[tawaf|طواف]] only around the cube.
If you do that, your [[tawaf|طواف]] is not valid,
because that is not the original structure, the original surface area of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. You have to go completely around the semicircle as well.
So that was one of the changes in the construction they had to make because of lack of funds. Another change that they made
is regarding the door of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. If you go to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] today,
you will see that it has one door. Those days, it used to have two doors.
One door on the side where you see it today and one door on the opposite side.
One door where you see it today and one door was on the opposite side as well.
And the people used to go in through one door and go out through the other door.
This was the common practice of the people: go in through the door that we have today, and go out through the door that was on the opposite side.
So they said, "Okay, we're not going to make the second door. We'll just make the first door."
And another thing that they decided to do is to elevate that door.
In those days, the door of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was on the ground level. But they decided, "No, we're not going to make it on the ground level. We're going to elevate it.
We're going to make it up."
And the reason why they decided to do this was so that they could control who goes in the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
They didn't want just anyone going inside the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
They said, "We're going to control who goes in the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] and who doesn't get to go in the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], so we're going to elevate that door."
So these were some of the changes that they made: one door, elevated the door, and the surface area of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was shortened,
and it was made into a cube shape instead of three sides straight and one side semicircle.
And the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], he had seen the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] how it was before, because this happened when he was 35 years old.
So he knows how the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was before that as well.

So he said, later on when he became powerful and after the conquest of [[Makkah|مكّة]], when the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] had control of [[Makkah|مكّة]], he could have ordered for it to be rebuilt as it was before,
but he said to [[Aishah|عائشة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], he said, "If it weren't for the fact that your people are new to Islam,"

many of those people of the [[Quraysh|قريش]], they just accepted Islam after the conquest of [[Makkah|مكّة]], after the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] came into [[Makkah|مكّة]] victorious,
and the conquest of [[Makkah|مكّة]] was complete.

Many of those people of [[Makkah|مكّة]] who were not Muslims before, they were the staunchest enemies of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] before, they became Muslim after that conquest of [[Makkah|مكّة]].
And they were new Muslims. And the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] wanted the [[Iman|إيمان]] to become stronger in their hearts.
So he said to [[Aishah|عائشة]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهَا]], "If it wasn't for the fact that your people," meaning the [[Quraysh|قريش]],
"if it wasn't for the fact that they are new to Islam, I would have rebuilt the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] again as it was"
on the foundations of [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], the way that it was before.
But he decided not to do that, and this shows the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], the wisdom. He decided not to do that because he thought
that it would cause [[fitnah|فتنة]] with the people. The Arabs, they're used to the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] the way that it is now.
If we change it, even though we're changing it actually back to the original form, if we change it, they may think that, "Oh, what is this? He changed the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]."
And they're new Muslims.
So he saw from his wisdom that it was better not to do this. And this again shows the intelligence and the wisdom of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]].
It also happened later on in history, during the time of [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]],

when [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]] was fighting [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج بن يوسف]], and [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج بن يوسف]] was striking at [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]] in [[Makkah|مكّة]] with catapults.
During that time, [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج بن يوسف]], he damaged the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with his attacks on [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]].
The [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was hit in the crossfire and the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was damaged.
So [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]], he rebuilt the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] as it originally was.
He rebuilt it with the semicircle portion included in the building, and he made two doors, and he made the door low instead of keeping it elevated.
So basically, he rebuilt it to the way that it was before the [[Quraysh|قريش]] rebuilt it. He rebuilt it in that way.
So it was restored to its original way at one point in history.
And then, when [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج]] got the upper hand and he got control of [[Makkah|مكّة]], he said, "Look what [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]] did."
"He played around with the house of Allah, and he messed up the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]."
And [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج]] ordered for it to be made back to the way it was, the way the [[Quraysh|قريش]] made it.
So it went back to that form again, the form that it is in today. [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج]] did that.
Then, when the [[khalifah|خليفة]] of the Muslims, [[Abdul Malik ibn Marwan|عبد الملك بن مروان]], when he heard about this,
he said, "No, no. What [[al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf|الحجاج]] did was wrong and what [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]] did was right."
So he said, "I'm going to make it back to that way again."
And then [[Imam Malik|إمام مالك]] [[rahimahullah|رَحِمَهُ اللهُ]], the great Imam, [[Imam Malik|إمام مالك بن أنس]],
he told [[Abdul Malik ibn Marwan|عبد الملك بن مروان]], he told the leader, he said, "Please, don't do it. Leave it. Leave it how it is."

And then [[Abdul Malik ibn Marwan|عبد الملك]] asked [[Imam Malik|إمام مالك]], he said, "But isn't the way that [[Abdullah ibn Zubayr|عَبْد الله بن الزُّبَيْر]] how he rebuilt it, isn't that how it originally was?
Isn't that the right way?" And [[Imam Malik|إمام مالك]] said, "Yes, that is the right way."
"But we cannot make the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] like a toy in the hands of the rulers.
This ruler decides to do this, and then this ruler decides to do that, and then this ruler decides to do that."
"We cannot make the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] a toy in the hands of the rulers. Just leave it how it is and don't touch it."
This was the [[hikmah|حكمة]] of [[Imam Malik|إمام مالك]] [[rahimahullah|رَحِمَهُ اللهُ]].
So [[Abdul Malik ibn Marwan|عبد الملك بن مروان]], he listened to this advice and he left it as it is, and it is still that way today.
The Saudi government, if they want to, they have enough money to rebuild it as it was before, they could do it. But they don't do it because of this reason,
because the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] cannot be like a toy with every ruler doing what he wants with it.
So this is the way it is, and this is the way that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] has decreed for it to be.
So this is the history of the rebuilding of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So once they finished the rebuilding, once they finished that rebuilding, there was one last step that needed to be made,
and that was placing [[al-Hajar al-Aswad|الحجر الأسود]], placing the black stone back into its corner, back into its place.
This is a great honor. Who's going to do this? We have many subtribes of the [[Quraysh|قريش]]:
[[Banu Abd al-Dar|بنو عبد الدار]], [[Banu Makhzum|بنو مخزوم]], so many different tribes, each one wants to have this honor for themselves.
So they start fighting over it, like who's going to get this honor, who's going to do it.
And it reached to such an extent where [[Banu Abd al-Dar|بنو عبد الدار]], they took a jug of blood, and each one of them put their hands into the blood.
Each member of that tribe, they put their hands in that blood,
and they said, "We swear, we swear that we are going to be the ones who put that stone in its place."
And when [[Banu Makhzum|بنو مخزوم]] saw what [[Banu Abd al-Dar|بنو عبد الدار]] were doing, they said, "Okay, we can do that too."
They got their own vessel of blood, and they put their hands in the blood, and they said, "We swear it will be someone from us, from our tribe, who is going to put that stone where it is."
So this is how much they regarded that being a great honor for them to put that stone in its place.
So the [[fitnah|فتنة]] became very intense, and they were ready to fight about it.
And then one wise old man, and his name was [[Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah|أبو أمية بن المغيرة]], he said, "Look..."
Why don't we just appoint someone to do it?
We will just appoint someone to do it, and everyone can agree who that person is going to be.
We select one person and he'll go ahead and do it on behalf of all of us.
And this was a wise old man, and out of respect for him, they said, "Okay, okay, we will agree to your way of getting out of this dilemma."
So then they thought to themselves and they started speaking among themselves, "Okay, who should we select? Who should do it?"
So then they decided, "Okay, we agree that the first person who comes in through [[Bab Bani Shaybah|باب بني شيبة]], the gate of [[Bani Shaybah|بني شيبة]]..."
And there were many gates of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] that people used to come in,
many gates around the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] where people used to enter the [[Haram|حرم]].
So they agreed among themselves, "The first man who walks in through [[Bab Bani Shaybah|باب بني شيبة]], through the gate of [[Bani Shaybah|بني شيبة]], he is the one who gets to do it."
So they waited, waited, looking at that gate, waiting for someone to come in.
And finally, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ walks through that gate.
And when he walks in, everyone is so happy. They say, "[[al-Sadiq al-Amin|الصَّادِق الأَمِين]]! [[al-Sadiq al-Amin|الصَّادِق الأَمِين]]! [[radina|رضينا]]! [[radina|رضينا]]!"
"The truthful one, the trustworthy one! The truthful one, the trustworthy one! We're happy with this, we're happy! Yes, he is the one who's going to do it."

So everyone was happy, because [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ had this reputation. Everybody loved him, everybody respected him, everybody honored him, and everyone knew how honorable and truthful and trustworthy he was.
So they were very happy.
that he is the one who came through that gate. So he comes in,
and he takes a cloth and he puts the [[al-Hajar al-Aswad|الحجر الأسود]] on that cloth.
And then he tells the leaders of these different sub-tribes of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]],
someone from [[Banu Makhzum|بَنِي مَخْزُوم]], someone from [[Banu Abd al-Dar|بَنِي عَبْد الدَّار]],
all of them, you hold a piece of that cloth where the stone is in the middle.
So each one of them, they hold around that cloth and they walk
towards the corner of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] where the stone is supposed to be placed.
So all of them are participating here. Nobody is left out. All of them are participating.
And then when they get near the corner, [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ⌨ with his blessed hand, he takes the stone and puts it in its place.
This again shows the [[hikmah|حكمة]] and the intelligence of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ⌨, how he diffused such a situation
and made everyone happy. They all participated in this way,
and [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ⌨ himself put that stone in its place. So this is the story
of the reconstruction of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] that happened five years before the first [[wahy|واف]] came to [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ⌨.
And this was when he was about thirty-five years old. [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] next week we will talk about
between thirty-five and forty. [[Wallahu a'lam|وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَم]].
between thirty-five and forty. [[Wallahu a'lam|وَاللهُ أَعْلَم]].

segments.en: And may Allah's peace, blessings and prayers be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.
segments.translit: wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ȹalā Nabiyyinā Muḥammad wa-ȹalā ālihī wa-ṣaḥbihī ajmaȹīn
